arxiv-1712-03198.title: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods Publication type: Tutorial in Biostatistics
arxiv-1712-03198.creator: Tim P Morris*, Ian R White, Michael J Crowther
arxiv-1712-03198.description: Abstract Simulation studies are computer experiments that involve creating data by pseudo-random sampling. A key strength of simulation studies is the ability to understand the behaviour of statistical methods because some ‘truth’ (usually some parameter/s of interest) is known from the process of generating the data. This allows us to consider properties of methods, such as bias.

arxiv-2204-10353.title: Invariants and chaos in the Volterra gyrostat without energy conservation Thanks: This paper is dedicated to the memory of Professor A S Vasudeva Murthy.
arxiv-2204-10353.creator: Ashwin K Seshadri, S Lakshmivarahan
arxiv-2204-10353.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ashwin K Seshadri, S Lakshmivarahan. The model of the Volterra gyrostat (VG) has not only played an important role in rigid body dynamics but also served as the foundation of low-order models of many naturally occurring systems. It is well known that VG possesses two invariants, or constants of motion, corresponding to kinetic energy and squared angular momentum, giving oscillatory solutions to its equations of motion.

arxiv-2210-09284.title: Large sets avoiding infinite arithmetic / geometric progressions Thanks: The third author was supported by the Hungarian National Research, Development ad Innovation Office - NKFIH, 124749 and 129335.
arxiv-2210-09284.creator: Alex Burgin, Samuel Goldberg, Tamás Keleti, Connor MacMahon, Xianzhi Wang
arxiv-2210-09284.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alex Burgin, Samuel Goldberg, Tamás Keleti, Connor MacMahon, Xianzhi Wang. We study some variants of the Erdős similarity problem. We pose the question if every measurable subset of the real line with positive measure contains a similar copy of an infinite geometric progression. We construct a compact subset E E of the real line such that 0 0 is a Lebesgue density point of E E , but E E does not contain any (non-constant) infinite geometric progression.

arxiv-2309-10414.title: Effects of plasma resistivity in three-dimensional full-F gyro-fluid turbulence simulations Journal: Plasma physics and controlled fusion
arxiv-2309-10414.creator: M. Wiesenberger, M. Held
arxiv-2309-10414.description: Abstract A full-F, isothermal, electromagnetic, gyro-fluid model is used to simulate plasma turbulence in a COMPASS-sized, diverted tokamak. A parameter scan covering three orders of magnitude of plasma resistivity and two values for the ion to electron temperature ratio with otherwise fixed parameters is setup and analysed.

arxiv-2310-20316.title: HWD: A Novel Evaluation Score for Styled Handwritten Text Generation
arxiv-2310-20316.creator: Vittorio Pippi, Fabio Quattrini, Silvia Cascianelli, Rita Cucchiara
arxiv-2310-20316.description: Abstract Styled Handwritten Text Generation (Styled HTG) is an important task in document analysis, aiming to generate text images with the handwriting of given reference images. In recent years, there has been significant progress in the development of deep learning models for tackling this task.

arxiv-2404-17251.title: Camera Motion Estimation from RGB-D-Inertial Scene Flow
arxiv-2404-17251.creator: Samuel Cerezo, Javier Civera
arxiv-2404-17251.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a novel formulation for camera motion estimation that integrates RGB-D images and inertial data through scene flow. Our goal is to accurately estimate the camera motion in a rigid 3D environment, along with the state of the inertial measurement unit (IMU).

arxiv-2410-23273.title: Proportional Fairness in Non-Centroid Clustering Thanks: A preliminary version will be published in the proceedings of the 38th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2024.
arxiv-2410-23273.creator: Ioannis Caragiannis, Evi Micha, Nisarg Shah
arxiv-2410-23273.description: Abstract We revisit the recently developed framework of proportionally fair clustering, where the goal is to provide group fairness guarantees that become stronger for groups of data points (agents) that are large and cohesive. Prior work applies this framework to centroid clustering, where the loss of an agent is its distance to the centroid assigned to its cluster.

arxiv-2412-09334.title: Assessing the replicability of RCTs in RWE emulations
arxiv-2412-09334.creator: Jeanette Köppe ∗, Charlotte Micheloud ∗, Stella Erdmann ∗, Rachel Heyard, Leonhard Held ∗ contributed equally Corresponding author: Jeanette Köppe: jeanette.koeppe@ukmuenster.de
arxiv-2412-09334.description: Abstract Abstract Background : The standard regulatory approach to assess replication success is the two-trials rule, requiring both the original and the replication study to be significant with effect estimates in the same direction. The sceptical p p -value was recently presented as an alternative method for the statistical assessment of the replicability of study results.

arxiv-2502-09462.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amalendu Krishna, Ritankar Nath. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14F43, Secondary 19D55 Abstract. One of these shows that for an algebraic space over a field acted upon by a linear algebraic group, the derived completion of equivariant K^{\prime} -theory at the augmentation ideal of the representation ring of the group coincides with the ordinary K^{\prime} -theory of the bar construction associated to the group

pmc-11495212.title: Quantifying the uniqueness and divisiveness of presidential discourse
pmc-11495212.creator: Karen Zhou, Alexander A Meitus, Milo Chase, Grace Wang, Anne Mykland, William Howell, Chenhao Tan, Katherine Ognyanova
pmc-11495212.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Do American presidents speak discernibly different from each other? And are these differences confined to any single medium of communication? To investigate these questions, this paper introduces a novel metric of uniqueness based on large language models, develops a new lexicon for divisive speech, and presents a framework for assessing the distinctive ways in which presidents speak about their political opponents.

pmc-12535531.title: Passive control of wing-tip vortices through a grooved-tip design
pmc-12535531.creator: Junchen Tan, Shūji Ōtomo, Ignazio Maria Viola, Yabin Liu
pmc-12535531.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper investigates the characteristics and control of tip vortices generated by a finite wing, focusing on the impact of the novel grooved-tip designs. Tip vortices can lead to flow loss, noise, vibration and cavitation in hydrodynamic systems. We propose and develop a grooved-tip design, featuring multiple grooves distributed along the wing tip to alter the tip vortex structure and dynamics. Four grooved-tip designs, including tilted and shrinking grooves, were experimentally investigated.

pmc-13214343.creator: Márton Eördögh, Martin Weidemeier, Gábor Baksa, Lajos Patonay, Daniel Simmen, Henry WS Schroeder, Ehab El Refaee, Werner Hosemann, Robert Reisch, Hans Rudolf Briner
pmc-13214343.description: IntroductionThe endoscopic transsphenoidal approach is the standard technique to remove central skull base lesions; however, binostril modifications often require extensive intranasal dissection resulting in sinonasal morbidity.Research questionThe transethmoid-paraseptal approach (TPA) is a mononostril alternative designed to preserve sinonasal function while maintaining adequate surgical exposure. Its systematic anatomical and radiological validation is lacking.

pmc-13320541.title: Insights from a multinational survey on ERC courses: a cross-sectional analysis of participant and instructor perspectives

Lockey, Robert Greif, Carsten Lott, John Madar, John Madar, Jana Djakow, Silvija Hunyadi-Anticevic, Patricia Conaghan, Nikolaos Nikolaou, Joachim Schlieber, Jacques Delchef, Marta Przybyl, Tanya Esposito, Elizabe
pmc-13320541.description: BackgroundEuropean Resuscitation Council (ERC) life support courses are delivered internationally to standardise resuscitation. Given advances in educational science, evolving learner needs, and rapid technological innovation, ongoing evaluation is required to ensure these courses continue to meet expectations. This study aimed to identify priorities for course delivery, teaching and assessment strategies, and to inform future course development.

pmc-13332601.title: Dexmedetomidine–remifentanil-assisted awake videolaryngoscopic intubation in a patient with Madelung disease and compensated liver cirrhosis undergoing prone lumbar spine surgery: a case report
pmc-13332601.creator: Jin-Wook Park, Jung Hee Choi
pmc-13332601.description: BackgroundMadelung disease (multiple symmetric lipomatosis) is a rare metabolic disorder characterized by progressive accumulation of non-encapsulated lipomatous tissue in the cervical and parapharyngeal regions, which can critically distort upper airway anatomy and substantially increase the risk of failed intubation. When a difficult airway is anticipated, awake tracheal intubation (ATI) is recommended.

pmc-13413313.title: Abdominal Aorta Balloon Occlusion Versus Standard Care in Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13413313.creator: Gauri Bapayeva, Meruyert Abdukassimova, Nazira Kadroldinova, Kuat Kassymbek, Karlygash Togyzbayeva, Lyazzat Saidildina, Viktor Zemlyanskiy, Kuanysh Balgynbayev, Mariya Usseyeva, Gulzhanat Aimagambetova, Milan Terzic
pmc-13413313.description: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is associated with substantial intraoperative hemorrhage. Abdominal aortic balloon occlusion (AABO) has been introduced to mitigate blood loss, though its benefit remains debated. This study, registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06721182), assessed maternal outcomes in women with PAS undergoing cesarean delivery managed either with abdominal aortic balloon occlusion or standard surgical care alone.

pmc-13573851.title: Dynamic Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Stratifies Survival and Immune-Related Adverse Events in Lung and Gastric Cancer Patients with Immunotherapy
pmc-13573851.creator: Chengcheng Qian, Mengting Wang, Chuyi Liu, Feng Liu, Wenying Zhang, Xiaohua Hu, Yanjie Zhang, Bin Jiang, Jiongyi Wang, Ming Xu, Haihua Yuan
pmc-13573851.description: BackgroundDynamic neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has emerged as a prognostic marker in immunotherapy outcomes, yet phase-specific alterations in NLR after immunotherapy and their association with treatment efficacy remain underreported. This study aimed to clarify the prognostic utility of NLR dynamics in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) therapy.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 101 cancer patients (including lung and gastric cancer) treated with ICIs.
